source: World Bank/ADB, 2004 Floods in Bangladesh: Damage and Needs Assessment and Proposed Recovery Program (via PreventionWeb)
note: First wave from July over about 33 districts; second wave in early September flooded Dhaka and the south-west and centre.

source: Government of Bangladesh Disaster Management Information Centre, Situation Report, Aug 2007 (ReliefWeb)
note: Floods from late July; UNICEF put 47 districts affected by 6 August; a second wave hit in mid-September (IRIN and UNICEF reports on ReliefWeb).

source: ACT Alliance, Alert: Bangladesh: Floods in Northern region (Aug 2017)
note: Severe flooding in 20 northern districts from 15 August, spreading to central districts; rivers receding by 21 August.

source: IFRC, Bangladesh: Monsoon Floods Emergency Plan of Action operation update no. 1 (MDRBD022), ReliefWeb
note: Heavy rain and upstream water from 7 July; 7.6 million people in 28 districts affected by 28 July.

source: ReliefWeb disaster page, Bangladesh: Floods and Landslides - Jul 2020 (FL-2020-000161-BGD)
note: Began late June; 30 districts and 5.4 million people affected by 11 August; over 60 days in some areas.

source: UN Resident Coordinator, Bangladesh 2022 Severe Flash Flood, Situation Update 1 (19 June 2022), ReliefWeb
note: About 94% of Sunamganj and 84% of Sylhet under water (FFWC); 4.3 million people in seven north-eastern districts.

source: UN OCHA, Bangladesh: Eastern Flash Flood Situation Report No. 01 (25 August 2024), ReliefWeb
note: Eleven districts from 21 August; worst hit Feni, Noakhali, Cumilla, Lakshmipur, Chattogram (Chattogram division) and Moulvibazar, Habiganj (Sylhet division).
